mission_05: MICE (Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations) is one of the most sophisticated imputation techniques available. It works by treating each variable with missing values as a target in turn, using all other variables as predictors. The process iterates multiple times, updating imputations in each round until convergence. This approach captures complex multivariate relationships and produces imputations that are consistent with the joint distribution of the data. sklearn IterativeImputer implements MICE and allows you to choose the underlying estimator, from BayesianRidge for linear relationships to RandomForestRegressor for non-linear patterns. MICE is the gold standard for missing data handling in statistical analysis and is recommended when missingness depends on observed variables (Missing at Random).
